parts.title: Startup and shutdown
parts.expect: The Windows executable loads modules, reaches the title frame and joins its workers at shutdown.

parts.title: Package integrity and portability
parts.expect: The package still starts after relocation. Missing or damaged modules and a missing decoder fail cleanly.

parts.title: Suspend and resume logic
parts.expect: Simulated sleep pauses the game clock and PCM. After resume, frames and audio continue from the previous position.

parts.title: Windows desktop integration
parts.expect: The ordinary window survives focus changes and real sleep and resume, and closes cleanly.
parts.gap: A repeatable desktop test on the current package is pending. Existing headless checks cover game logic and the framebuffer.

parts.title: Framebuffer and display
parts.expect: Tests check pixel format, stride, frame capture and GDI pixels in memory.

parts.title: Opening sequence
parts.expect: Compare all 319 RGB frames of the recorded opening sequence.

parts.title: Title interface
parts.expect: The title menu starts normal transitions. Tests verify rendering and the circular reveal.

parts.title: Fonts and dialogue
parts.expect: Dialogue and choices pass display tests. Menus and inventory are exercised through their own renderers.

parts.title: Geometry and lighting
parts.expect: Checks cover home scene rendering and TV-driven light changes in controlled states.

parts.title: Rigs and motion
parts.expect: All five models load, play the selected commands and report readiness.

parts.title: KSC and DAK effects
parts.expect: Selected EF1–EF4 and EF9 effects are checked for appearance and cleanup.

parts.title: Camera and occlusion
parts.expect: Selected camera transitions and approach branches execute in the room renderer.

parts.title: Materials, frame boundaries and scenes
parts.expect: Compare frames or numeric invariants across active scenes, periods, materials, transparency, shadows, occlusion and animation boundaries.
parts.gap: The scene and phase matrix is incomplete. Some materials and scenes still lack functional coverage.

parts.title: Layout, input edges and focus
parts.expect: Button mapping and software recovery after loss of focus or device pass regression checks.

parts.title: Menu and editor input
parts.expect: Checks cover routing buttons in menus, entering words, editing readings, confirming and cancelling.

parts.title: Physical controller
parts.expect: A physical XInput controller operates the menu and game and recovers after reconnection.
parts.gap: The software adapter passed. No physical controllers were detected on the test system.

parts.title: Decoder and native worker
parts.expect: The native worker produces nonzero PCM after startup. The check uses a null sink.

parts.title: Music and events
parts.expect: A music voice starts at the correct title event and changes to the next track.

parts.title: Queues and voices
parts.expect: Tests verify duration, pause, looping, volume and voice completion through the null sink.

parts.title: Mixing and full event catalog
parts.expect: Compare reference PCM across game event groups, voice completion and concurrent audio channels.
parts.gap: Selected streams and scenarios are covered. The full event catalog, overlapping voices and edge cases still lack an integrated matrix.

parts.title: Activity, clocks and wait cancellation
parts.expect: Selected room scenarios check activity choice, conditional repeats, timers and return of control.

parts.title: Ordinary topics for all five characters
parts.expect: All 3118 ordinary entries return control. A scripted topic change after declining an entry is counted separately.

parts.title: Special and alternate KSC paths
parts.expect: Trace command and procedure outcomes across vocabulary states, dates, answers and locations. Distinguish expected declines from unsupported paths.
parts.gap: Ordinary topics and selected special paths are listed. The procedure, outcome and transition inventory for all five characters is incomplete.

parts.title: Room objects and options
parts.expect: The actual components handle selected TV changes, item placement and the in-game options screen.

parts.title: Learning and reusing a word
parts.expect: Tests cover acceptance, refusal and selecting an accepted word again in conversation.

parts.title: Keyboards and reading edits
parts.expect: Test layouts, grouped entry, confirm, cancel and reading updates.

parts.title: Conversion and query history
parts.expect: Check single and compound queries, classes, reading limits and competing analyses.

parts.title: Notebook and diary
parts.expect: Tests check vocabulary and tabs. A room test verifies the first diary entry is created and retained in state.

parts.title: Vocabulary categories and limits
parts.expect: Cover all word and morpheme classes, refusals, empty and full vocabularies, history and saving for all five characters.
parts.gap: Differential conversion and lesson tests cover a subset of the possible combinations.

parts.title: Inventory lifecycle
parts.expect: Check the active slot, placement and storage, discard confirm and decline, gift marking and filtering.

parts.title: Home menu
parts.expect: A focused test verifies opening options, applying, cancelling and returning control.

parts.title: Roof and return
parts.expect: The KSC scenario checks departure, roof and return requests. A room component loads roof resources separately.

parts.title: Travel resources
parts.expect: A test loads 54 scene registrations and renders each in both buffers.

parts.title: Travel by character and season
parts.expect: Eligible destinations are reachable by all five characters with valid inputs. Menus, tasks, return and repeat outings work at the location.
parts.gap: Toro's 15 ordinary trips and two round trips to each alternate character's default destination passed. The alternate routes also cover cancellation and a new activity after returning home. The alternate destinations, seasonal coverage and location-specific tasks are still open.

parts.title: Character selection and profile fields
parts.expect: Dedicated tests check the form, dates, field handoff and carousel images.

parts.title: Toro and the first gift
parts.expect: The introduction, gift and initial conversations return control to the room.

parts.title: Robo's calendar scenes
parts.expect: Selected introduction, saving, penultimate day and farewell tests reach their expected returns.

parts.title: Usagi's calendar scenes
parts.expect: Selected introduction, saving, penultimate day and farewell tests reach their expected returns.

parts.title: Inu's calendar scenes
parts.expect: Selected introduction, saving, penultimate day and farewell tests reach their expected returns.

parts.title: Kaeru's calendar scenes
parts.expect: Selected introduction, saving, penultimate day and farewell tests reach their expected returns.

parts.title: Toro's calendar state
parts.expect: Next-day cases and the room graph preserve the calendar and diary data.

parts.title: Toro, GAME37 and GAME75
parts.expect: A fresh slot reaches the penultimate day, both endings, cold loading and Continue on the tested build.
parts.evidence: A fresh Toro profile went from the title to the first save, successive dates and the penultimate scene. Day 14 and day 24 branched from the same slot and each cold-loaded into the empty room. Extension prerequisites were set at the branch.

parts.title: Scheduled letter (event 7)
parts.expect: The scheduled letter, return to player control and a later cold load work for all applicable characters.
parts.evidence: All 10 prepared-slot routes passed: cold entry and a day change in the active room, two routes for each of the five characters.

parts.title: Departure and starting a new stay
parts.expect: A departed slot opens the empty room. Re-adoption preserves vocabulary and cards after a cold load.
parts.evidence: Toro's departure led to the empty room, Robo adoption and a normal save. A cold load verified the word and reopened a friend card. The input was a local slot and the card was supplied by the test.

parts.title: Save graph and slot format
parts.expect: Check serialization, integrity, payload protection and controlled rejection of damaged data.

parts.title: Saving from the room and restoring
parts.expect: Robo, Usagi, Inu and Kaeru write a protected slot from the room. Cold loading restores state. Graph and inventory formats are checked separately.

parts.title: Atomic save and recovery
parts.expect: The matrix covers damage to each file, failures in each replacement phase, access denial and cold loading again.
parts.evidence: Tests covered corruption, missing files and staging damage across all six members, 11 exceptions, 11 process exits and six Windows sharing conflicts. Cold processes checked the recovered generation and file integrity.

parts.title: Discovery, isolation and protocol
parts.expect: Windows processes on loopback check session matching, transfer, location and mode isolation, and tampering rejection.

parts.title: Meeting offers and eligibility
parts.expect: Check prepared questions, shiritori eligibility and leaving the menu through the implemented routes.

parts.title: Friend card, notebook and save
parts.expect: Two processes complete the exchange. Both received cards appear after each process restarts.
parts.evidence: Two local Windows processes exchanged cards and saved. After separate cold starts all 30 fields of the received cards matched and both cards opened in the notebook. Cancelling while waiting was checked separately.

parts.title: Gift exchange, cancellation and atomicity
parts.expect: Across two processes, exchanges and cancellations affect only the intended slots and remain consistent after failure or reload.
parts.evidence: Tests covered a bilateral gift swap, cancelling without a partner, and aborting after both players prepared but before applying the swap. All 170 inventory rows and six slot files per player were checked after cold loading.

parts.title: Shiritori match and exit
parts.expect: Check offers, wins, losses, cancellation, invalid moves and return to autonomous play.
parts.evidence: Game-menu offer, wins and losses on loopback, and cancellation without a partner passed. Invalid links, repeats and final ん were sent through the test channel and rejected. All cases restored room control and saved word flags were checked.

parts.title: Two independent Windows hosts
parts.expect: Peer discovery and exchange work across Windows hosts on an ordinary network, including loss of connectivity.
parts.gap: Loopback passed. This suite has yet to run across two independent Windows hosts.

parts.title: Actor readiness, input, frame and activity
parts.expect: One room controller handles the actor turn, button choices and dialogue. A new autonomous activity starts after return. Frames render to both buffers.

parts.title: Startup, profile and room
parts.expect: A headless route exercises the native game loop from the first frame through profile acceptance and an autonomous room activity.
parts.evidence: A fresh Windows EXE session loaded nine modules, produced a visible frame, accepted all seven fields, completed Toro's introduction and gift, and finished an autonomous activity.

parts.title: Conversation, vocabulary, notebook and save
parts.expect: One route learns a word, opens the notebook, creates a slot and verifies the same spelling and reading in a new process.
parts.evidence: Robo's ordinary conversation taught the word. Row 163 was present in the live notebook before saving. A second cold process verified the spelling and reading and all six files matched.

parts.title: Menu, destination and return
parts.expect: A headless path opens the menu, changes scenes and restores control and the next activity at home.
parts.evidence: All 15 ordinary Toro destinations passed: menu, rendered scene, activity away from home, manual return and activity at home. Eligibility was prepared in memory.

parts.title: Save, date rollover, event and resave
parts.expect: One test covers date changes, the end of the stay and two cold loads with ordinary controls at both checkpoints.
parts.evidence: A fresh Toro profile recovered the previous protected save on cold startup, crossed November 30 to December 1 in the running room, and saved again through System. The same slot advanced through day 14 and the farewell. A separate cold process opened the departed room through Continue.

parts.title: Meeting, game result and cold reload
parts.expect: Two players' state survives connection, a completed or cancelled operation, saving and loading again.
parts.evidence: The same two slots completed card exchange, prepared gift cancellation, successful gift exchange and shiritori. Normal saves linked the stages. Both independent cold processes opened the cards, inventories and words without changing files.

parts.title: Feature and transition inventory completeness
parts.expect: Compare the requirements against the original scene, command, transition, module and menu tables. Every player-accessible route has a test or an expected outcome.
parts.gap: The current 68-feature inventory describes known coverage. The full graph of player-accessible routes is still unverified.

scope: Local Windows Release acceptance snapshot, executed without windows or audio output.

game-return-letter.scope: Windows Release, headless, null audio, locally prepared day-three slots, cold entry and one-second midnight transition.

game-readoption.scope: Windows Release, headless, null audio, completed Toro slot with a learned word and a controlled friend card. Empty room, title, Robo adoption, System save and independent cold notebook.

game-out-and-back.scope: Windows Release, headless, null audio. Toro's ordinary destinations, eligibility prepared in memory, native menu and return with a new activity in both scenes.

game-startup-to-room.scope: Windows Release, fresh temporary installation with local media and decoder. Normal startup worker and game frame path, no window, null audio, midday room clock and controlled input.

game-contact-to-save.scope: Windows Release, headless, null audio. Controlled Robo room calendar and inputs, native contact and lesson, memo, System save, separate process cold load and exact slot preservation.

game-peer-card.scope: Windows Release, headless, null audio. Loopback card exchange with System Save and two cold processes, plus no-partner cancellation, on local protected Toro fixtures.

game-peer-gift.scope: Windows Release, headless, null audio. Loopback gift exchange, no-partner cancellation and bilateral prepared abort before commit; five cold processes and intact six-file slots.

game-peer-shiritori.scope: Windows Release, headless, null audio. One two-player loopback match, no-partner cancellation and three rejected moves at the game channel boundary, with room return and persisted word-use checks.

game-seam-links.scope: Windows Release, headless, null audio. One linked four-visit route with two protected slots on loopback. Controlled cancellation before commit; System menu saves between operations, then two separate cold loads.

game-save-recovery.scope: Windows Release, independent headless processes, null audio. Local protected donor and two test generations. Six files with three fault cases each, 11 thrown faults, 11 process exits, six sharing denials, and orphan staging and backup checks.

game-toro-ending.scope: Windows Release, headless, null audio. Fresh Toro adoption and native daily saves; ordinary and extended endings branched from day 13. Controlled time, answers and extended-stay qualification before the fork; cold Continue in both branches.

game-seam-calendar.scope: Windows Release, headless and null audio. Four independent processes used the same temporary installation. A real System save was staged as the previous generation with an incomplete sibling. Recovery preserved all six files. Controlled in-game month rollover, diary, days 2–14, farewell and cold Continue with restricted room controls.

game-starting-outings.scope: Windows Release, headless and null audio. Independent new rooms for Robo, Usagi, Inu and Kaeru each wrote the source-backed initial destination flag in a protected System save. Robo retained the flag through a day-two save.

game-named-outings.scope: Windows Release, headless and null audio. Fresh protected saves, four cancellations and eight round trips across Robo, Usagi, Inu and Kaeru. Ordered departure motions, rendered arrivals, away activities, manual return and new home activities. Usagi's route uses a controlled learned word.
